supporting: type conversion at a conceptual level

claims.claim: JavaScript has primitive values including undefined, null, boolean, number, bigint, string, and symbol.
An expression is a unit of code that resolves to a value, while a statement performs an action.
Arithmetic operators combine numeric operands and comparison operators produce Boolean results.
JavaScript source text contains statements, and expression statements evaluate an expression and discard its completion value.
Comments are ignored by the JavaScript engine and can explain intent for people reading source code.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft was generic boilerplate and was replaced.
correctionsNeeded: Defined primitive values without introducing variables, functions, arrays, or objects.
rightsIssues: MDN and ECMA-262 were used as reference-only sources; all lesson prose is original synthesis.
